import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1024

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1024](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1024)
- [PhRo86] Phelps, K. T. and R\"odl, V., Steiner triple systems with minimum independence number. Ars
  Combin. (1986), 167--172.
-/

namespace Erdos1024

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Let $f(n)$ be such that every $3$-uniform linear hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains an independent
set on $f(n)$ vertices. Estimate $f(n)$.

Phelps and Rödl [PhRo86] proved $f(n) \asymp (n\log n)^{1/2}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1024 :
    (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.linearIndependenceNumber n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
    (answer(fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.sqrt (n * Real.log n))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1024

reformulations.difference: The source describes the optimal universally guaranteed independent-set size verbally. Lean uses Hypergraph.linearIndependenceNumber, encoded as n minus the maximum of n minus the independence number over admissible labelled edge families.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The enumerated families are exactly the linear three-uniform hypergraphs on Fin n, and the class is nonempty because it contains the empty edge family. Every independence number is at most n, so n − max_H(n − α(H)) equals min_H α(H), with no truncated-subtraction anomaly. Independence numbers are attained and independence is preserved under taking subsets. Consequently, k ≤ linearIndependenceNumber n iff every admissible hypergraph has an independent set of exactly k vertices. This equivalence was proved in Review1024.guarantee_iff in the scratch file. Relabelling vertices by Fin n imposes no restriction. The scratch file also proves that the displayed Θ relation is equivalent to eventual two-sided bounds with fixed positive constants.

review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and all relevant shared definitions. The answer has type ℕ → ℝ and supplies exactly the source’s growth rate. Boundary tests give linearIndependenceNumber n = 0,1,2,2,3,4 for n = 0,…,5. The zero values of log/sqrt at n = 0 and n = 1 do not affect a Θ statement at natural-number atTop. Semantic equivalence proofs and boundary tests compile cleanly in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the equivalence proofs do not depend on sorryAx. The full text of PhRo86 was not obtainable from the publisher/author pages, but the cited problem page explicitly states the exact bound used here, so the declaration’s faithfulness could be settled.
